title: Sowing kale microgreens
subtitle: How to fill, sow, and start the blackout phase for a kale microgreen tray
excerpt: Kale microgreens are sown using the standard brassica method: no pre-treatment, scatter seed at 15 to 20 g per 25 cm tray, press into contact with the medium, and blackout. Kale is slightly slower to germinate than radish or broccoli, emerging in three to four days.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine-textured, low-fertility growing medium designed for germination. Seed compost has smaller particles than multi-purpose compost, which helps seeds make even contact with the medium surface. Use it for microgreen trays rather than multi-purpose compost.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. For kale, expect three to four days before the shoots are ready to move to light.

content.text: Kale microgreens are sown using the standard brassica sowing method: no pre-soak, no hull treatment. Kale seed is slightly larger and darker than broccoli seed and germinates a day or two more slowly, but the process is identical. The method below applies to all curly and flat-leaved kale varieties.

One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray. A second tray for the blackout cover. Seed compost. A watering can or jug. Kale seed: 15 to 20 g per tray. A flat piece of card or the base of the second tray for pressing.

Step 1: pre-dampen the compost. Add water to the seed compost and mix until it holds together when squeezed but does not drip. Pre-dampening before filling the tray prevents needing to water after sowing.
is better for microgreens than multi-purpose compost. The finer texture lets seeds lie flat and germinate evenly.
Step 2: fill the tray with pre-dampened compost to within 1 cm of the rim. Level the surface with a straight edge or the flat of your hand.
Step 3: scatter kale seed at 15 to 20 g per tray. Kale seed is slightly larger than broccoli seed and scatters readily. Work in systematic rows from 15 to 20 cm above the tray surface.
Step 4: press. Use the flat base of the second tray or a piece of card to press the seed into firm contact with the medium across the whole tray surface.
: stack the second tray on top with a light weight. Kale germinates in three to four days; check at day 3 for upright shoots at 2 to 3 cm before moving to light.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with kale microgreens.

items.cause: Seed not in contact with the medium, room too cold, or old seed.
items.fix: Press more firmly on the next attempt. Confirm room temperature is above 15°C. Use seed from the current or previous season.

items.symptom: Patchy coverage with dense clusters and bare areas
items.fix: Scatter in small pinches across the tray in systematic rows, moving steadily.
